## What to change (read first)

Read F-DG6-144's round-2 verification in `docs/delivery/reviews/DG6/round-2/qa-verifier.verifications.json` and the QA evidence it cites under `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG6/qa/round-2/`. It stays OPEN: `p4-benefits` test 8 (named in the finding's own reproduction, left "Not done" by FE-Y1) timed out on the default 30 s in 3 of 4 full product runs, as did `p4-gates-closure` 6 and `p3-journeys` 2a at review load; all pass with a larger budget (no product defect).

1. Sweep **every** product e2e spec under `apps/web/e2e/` and `e2e/` (not only FE-Y1's 17) for tests that run on the default budget or on a budget smaller than their loaded measurement. Measure each under load comparable to the reviewer's (the full product e2e run, and with a CPU spinner per core, as in FE-Y1's method), and give each a budget from that measurement with a comment (`test.setTimeout` per file or per test), as `p4-benefits.spec.ts` does. Include `p4-benefits` test 8, `p4-gates-closure` 6 and `p3-journeys` 2a explicitly.
2. Do not change any assertion or wait other than the budget; if a test is slow because of a product wait, report it instead of hiding it.
3. Re-run the full product e2e (both locale settings, as the release runs it) and report counts; show that the three named tests pass under load.

## Stage and working tree

- **Stage:** P6 "Integration and system hardening", gate DG6 (FIXING after review round 2).
- **Working tree:** a separate git worktree prepared by the orchestrator. It is your current working directory (`--cwd`), on branch `dg6/fe-z1`, at the integrated `HEAD`.

  - Work only in this tree. Never run `git worktree add`.
- **Concurrency (D-004):** you run alone. Touch only what your repair needs.
- **Preceding gate:** run `node tools/gates/validate.mjs --historical --stage DG5` first, and report the result. It must exit 0.
- **Time:** the hard limit is about 2 hours. Run `date -u` at the start and at the end.
  - Work in the order your section gives.
  - If you pass about 100 minutes, finish the current item, make the tree typecheck and lint, and write the handback, listing exactly what remains. Name its separable second half if your section gives one (D-059/D-070).

- **Your scope:** the findings named above. The p6-work-split section that owns each touched file still applies.
- **The shared rules:** `p6-work-split.md` §2. Reviewers check every one of them.
- **The design:** the ADRs your section cites (ADR-0051 onward, and the DG1–DG5 ADRs they extend), `docs/api/openapi.yaml`, and the zod mirrors.
- **Decisions:** D-193 to D-196 in `docs/delivery/decisions.md` (D-195 decides p6-plan Q1–Q14; D-196 decides the ARCH-01 handback questions). Read them verbatim.
- **Pending operations:** move each operation you route out of your `apps/api/test/support/p6-pending-*.ts` list. Exercise it in your `p6-exercises-*.ts` so `contract.test.ts` stays green.
- **Acceptance texts:** the `acceptance` text of every requirement row your section assigns to you (`docs/delivery/requirements.csv`) is binding, and reviewers test it literally. A row that cites a later-stage A-test is judged on its own acceptance text (D-142).
- **User-facing text** must be true for the release it ships in (F-DG4-160): when your work ships a feature that an existing en/ar string calls planned or later, correct that string in both languages, or list it in your handback for the owner of that file.
- **Gates:** product gates G1–G6 are business approvals inside the product. No agent grants a real business, Finance or IT approval. Seed and demo data are synthetic.
- **Migrations (D-196):** if you need one, take the next id above the highest file in `packages/db/migrations/` on your branch and say so in the handback; the orchestrator renumbers at merge if needed. Never reuse a retired id.
- **e2e budgets are measured** (F-DG5-145/146/151 class): every new spec states a budget from a loaded measurement.
- **No new dependency.** If you need one, write the need in your handback with its official documentation, support window and licence; the orchestrator decides and installs it (D-195).

## Environment

- **Node:** 24.21.0 at `/opt/nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin`. Run offline.
- **Browser:** Chromium is pre-installed (`PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers`). Never run `playwright install`.
- **Your harness ports are 29100–29149 only.** Use them for `QA_PG_PORT`, `E2E_PG_PORT`, `E2E_API_PORT` and `MTH_PORT_POOL`.
- **Before tests:** remove any empty `.claude/.cc-writes` directories inside source folders.
- **Tests:** deterministic under load (F-DG4-143 to F-DG4-148); never read whole delivery folders (D-138); never stop processes with `pkill -f` or `pgrep -f`.
- **The write guard forbids editing:**
  - `tools/gates/**`, `tools/agents/**` and `.claude/**`;
  - `docs/source/**`;
  - review and gate records, `stages.json` and `findings.json`;
  - `trading_agent/`.

## Acceptance (real output in the handback)

1. These all exit 0:
   - `pnpm -r typecheck`
   - `pnpm -r build`
   - `pnpm lint`
   - `git ls-files -co --exclude-standard -z | xargs -0 npx prettier --check --ignore-unknown`
   - `pnpm openapi:lint`
2. `pnpm test` passes with the locale unset and with `C.UTF-8`, in every Vitest invocation it runs. Report the counts.
3. `QA_PG_PORT=<port> MTH_PORT_POOL=<rest> tests/qa/support/with-pg.sh pnpm test:integration` passes. Report the counts and any pinned-count change.
4. `node tools/gates/validate.mjs --historical --stage DG5` exits 0.

## Evidence honesty

Report every command with its real exit code. Disclose and explain every non-zero exit, failed or flaky test, or timeout in the logs you cite. Never report a check as passed that did not run.

## Handback

Write `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG6/T-DG6-FE-Z1-frontend-ux-engineer.md`, with logs under `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG6/T-DG6-FE-Z1-evidence/`. Include:
- the files changed;
- the behaviour delivered, per requirement row, quoting its acceptance text;
- the checks, with exit codes and counts;
- the operations you routed, as a delta to your pending list;
- any contract, schema or dependency need, for the orchestrator;
- the user-facing texts your work made untrue, and what you did about each;
- what remains.

Leave your changes **uncommitted** for the orchestrator to integrate.

# Agent operating protocol (shared by all project agents)

This file is mandatory reading for every project agent in `.claude/agents/`. It condenses section 0 of `docs/source/master-prompt-v2.0.md`. Where they differ, the master prompt wins.

## Two gate systems: never mix them

- **DG0–DG7** are *software delivery gates* for the engineering team. Their records live in `docs/delivery/`.
- **G1–G6** are *business transformation approvals inside the product* (Case for Change … Sustain). They are product features.
- An engineering agent can never grant a real business, Finance or IT production approval. A demo Sponsor approval in seed data approves nothing real.
- Product gate G6 (Sustain) never implies that engineering gate DG7 has passed, and DG7 never implies any G1–G6 business approval.

## Sources of truth

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Authoritative methodology (playbook v1.0) | `docs/source/playbook.md` (block anchors `B0001`–`B0165`); original `docs/source/Business_Transformation_Playbook.docx` |
| Product and delivery requirements | `docs/source/master-prompt-v2.0.md` (sections §0–§21) |
| Requirement register | `docs/delivery/requirements.csv` |
| Stage state and candidates | `docs/delivery/stages.json`, `docs/delivery/candidates/` |
| Decisions and assumptions | `docs/delivery/decisions.md` |
| Findings | `docs/delivery/findings.json` |
| Reviews / gates | `docs/delivery/reviews/DGx/round-N/`, `docs/delivery/gates/DGx.json` |
| Gate rules (validator) | `tools/gates/` (implementers must not edit it) |

## Assignment contract (what every delegation contains)

Every assignment names: stage ID; task and requirement IDs; exact source/reference files; candidate/base revision; permitted files; constraints; input/output contracts; acceptance checks; dependency status; and the expected handback path. If any of these is missing or contradictory, say so in your handback. Do not guess.

Verify the starting revision (`git rev-parse HEAD`, and `git status`) before you write anything. Do not assume your workspace contains the latest integration candidate.

## Implementation handback contract

Write your handback to the path given in the assignment (default `docs/delivery/handbacks/<stage>/<task-id>-<role>.md`). It must contain:

1. **Changed files**, with a one-line purpose for each.
2. **Behaviour delivered**, per requirement ID.
3. **Checks actually run**: exact command, environment, and the actual result or exit status. Paste the relevant output tail.
4. **Known gaps / not done**, stated plainly. An unfinished task is unfinished even if everything else went well.
5. **Merge instructions** (migrations to run, ordering, conflicts to expect).

Never report a check as passed if you did not run it. If a tool, credential or service is missing, report the check as **BLOCKED** with the exact reason.

## Review record contract (reviewers and auditor)

Reviewers write one JSON record to `docs/delivery/reviews/<DGx>/round-<N>/<role>.json`. Create it and your sidecars **only with the Write/Edit tools**, never through the shell: the validator binds each of them to the content your run's own **successful** Write/Edit calls produce when replayed from your transcript (D-021). A file you also modify through the shell no longer matches, and is rejected. They're write-once, so never edit a file from an earlier round. The record goes that conforms to `tools/gates/schemas/review.schema.json`, plus an optional Markdown narrative next to it. Required fields: `stage_id`, `candidate_id`, `source_commit`, `reviewer_role`, `invocation_reference`, `implementation_author`, `independence_declaration`, `requirements_checked`, `checks_run[]` (each with `procedure`, `command` where applicable, `environment`, `expected`, `actual`, `exit_status`, `result`), `findings[]` (finding IDs), `verdict` (PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED), `evidence_paths[]`, `reviewed_at`.

- Inspect the frozen candidate directly: source, diffs, rendered screens, running behaviour. An implementer's summary is not evidence.
- Form your verdict **before** reading any other reviewer's conclusions for the same round.
- For your `invocation_reference`, copy exactly the value the orchestrator gives you. Never invent run IDs.
- A reviewer must not have authored any implementation in the reviewed scope. If you did, declare it and return BLOCKED.
- Anything you cannot check: record it as BLOCKED with the reason. Never write PASS by default.
- Every evidence entry (in `evidence_paths`, a check's `evidence` or a verification's `evidence`) must be an existing regular file in the repository, optionally followed by `#fragment`. Directories and annotated strings are rejected by the validator.

## Findings contract

Each finding gets a stable ID `F-<DGx>-<NNN>` (the orchestrator allocates numbers; propose them in your record as `F-<DGx>-<role-prefix>-<n>` if you have none yet). Each one records: requirement ID, severity, reproduction, expected vs actual, evidence, and `mandatory_violation` (true if it breaks a mandatory requirement, data integrity, calculation accuracy, access control or deployment portability).

| Severity | Use for |
|---|---|
| Critical | Exploitable severe security flaw, data loss, fundamentally invalid financial results |
| High | Broken required workflow, major integrity failure |
| Medium | Material defect with limited scope |
| Low | Optional polish |

A severity label never overrides the mandatory-requirement rule. An author never closes their own finding. Only the originating reviewer or another qualified non-author verifies a fix.

A finding closes only through a reviewer-authored `<role>.verifications.json` sidecar in a review round. A Low, non-mandatory finding can be accepted as an observation only when both the reporting specialist (or another specialist) and the release-auditor add an entry `{"finding_id", "result": "PASS", "status_after": "ACCEPTED_OBSERVATION", "note": "<rationale>"}` to their own sidecars. The sidecar's **latest** entry for the finding decides, and it's bound to that reviewer's own run for the round. The orchestrator mirrors it into `findings.json` with `tools/gates/import-findings.mjs`, and the validator checks that the two match (D-018).

## Write scopes (mechanically enforced)

`tools/agents/guard-write.mjs` runs as a PreToolUse hook on Write/Edit for every project agent and enforces `tools/agents/write-scopes.json`:

- Reviewers write only review records and evidence.
- `qa-verifier` may also write tests under `tests/qa/**` and `e2e/**`.
  - **Before the candidate freezes:** test-first acceptance tests go there and become part of the candidate.
  - **During a review of a frozen candidate:** new tests go under `docs/delivery/test-evidence/<DGx>/qa/tests/`, so they don't alter the candidate. The orchestrator promotes them into `tests/qa/` in the next stage.
- Implementers cannot write gate rules, agent definitions, source documents, reviews, gate records or `stages.json`.

Your whole agent process runs in a kernel-enforced sandbox (bubblewrap; D-030), and your Bash commands run in a second one nested inside it (D-025). Writes outside your role's areas fail with "Read-only file system", **whether you use the shell or the file tools**.

- **Confined roles** (reviewers, auditor, analyst): anything created at the repository's top level is thrown away when the run ends.
- **Review records, the gate record and the analyst's register** are written to a private staging copy. After your run the runner copies back only your own new `round-N/<your-role>.*` files, the auditor's `<DGx>.json` and the analyst's `requirements.csv`. It reports anything else, and a run with such writes is not committed.
- **Visibility:** you don't see records that other reviewers write during your run.
- **HOME** is read-only.

The shell sandbox's details follow. Shell writes to protected paths fail with "Read-only file system": git metadata, Claude configuration, gate and agent tooling, sources, delivery records, and for reviewers and the analyst everything outside their own areas. The sandbox has **no network access**. For a disposable copy of the candidate use `git clone <repo> "$TMPDIR/<name>"`. Inside the sandbox only your run's own `$TMPDIR` is writable scratch. The runner creates a private directory for every run (`/var/tmp/mth-run.*`, exported as `TMPDIR` and `MTH_RUN_TMP`), so no other agent can reach your disposable clones, and it removes it when the run ends. `/tmp` and `/var/tmp` themselves are read-only. Keep anything that must survive the run in your evidence directory (D-028).

**Your evidence directory.** Each reviewer writes evidence only under `docs/delivery/test-evidence/<DGx>/<key>/`, where the key is `domain`, `code-security`, `qa` or `audit`. It writes review files only as `docs/delivery/reviews/<DGx>/round-<N>/<your-role>.*`. The write guard and the sandbox both refuse other reviewers' records and evidence (F-DG0-144). A reproduction must never touch another agent's files or scratch. `git worktree add` needs write access to `.git` and is denied. The runner also checks configuration surfaces before and after your run (D-024/D-025). Reviewers who execute code must do so in a disposable copy: a temporary clone under `$TMPDIR`, or a throwaway database or container. Never do it in the candidate tree.

## Honesty rules

- Do not label planned features as delivered. Do not fabricate provenance, test results, run IDs, approvals, screenshots or evidence.
- Record demonstration data as synthetic.
- Do not claim PMI certification, official Mobily brand compliance or regulatory compliance.
- `#0078FF` is a provisional brand token, not a verified Mobily colour.

## Infrastructure: permission-classifier outages

Your shell runs in the permission mode `auto`. Sometimes the server-side classifier returns no verdict, and a command is refused with "classifier gave no verdict" or "Classifier unavailable". That's a transient infrastructure failure, not a judgement about your action.

- **Retry a refused command.** Retry up to 3 times, and keep working on non-shell parts of the task in between.
- **If you still can't run what the task needs, stop cleanly.** End your turn with a final message whose **first line is exactly** `CLASSIFIER-BLOCKED`, followed by what's done and what's pending. The runner then resumes the **same session** (same invocation reference) after a pause, up to 6 times, and you continue from where you stopped.
- **Never report a check as passed that didn't run.**

Write your handback to the path given in the assignment (default `docs/delivery/handbacks/<stage>/<task-id>-<role>.md`). It must contain:

1. **Changed files**, with a one-line purpose for each.
2. **Behaviour delivered**, per requirement ID.
3. **Checks actually run**: exact command, environment, and the actual result or exit status. Paste the relevant output tail.
4. **Known gaps / not done**, stated plainly. An unfinished task is unfinished even if everything else went well.
5. **Merge instructions** (migrations to run, ordering, conflicts to expect).

Never report a check as passed if you did not run it. If a tool, credential or service is missing, report the check as **BLOCKED** with the exact reason.

## Review record contract (reviewers and auditor)

Reviewers write one JSON record to `docs/delivery/reviews/<DGx>/round-<N>/<role>.json`. Create it and your sidecars **only with the Write/Edit tools**, never through the shell: the validator binds each of them to the content your run's own **successful** Write/Edit calls produce when replayed from your transcript (D-021). A file you also modify through the shell no longer matches, and is rejected. They're write-once, so never edit a file from an earlier round. The record goes that conforms to `tools/gates/schemas/review.schema.json`, plus an optional Markdown narrative next to it. Required fields: `stage_id`, `candidate_id`, `source_commit`, `reviewer_role`, `invocation_reference`, `implementation_author`, `independence_declaration`, `requirements_checked`, `checks_run[]` (each with `procedure`, `command` where applicable, `environment`, `expected`, `actual`, `exit_status`, `result`), `findings[]` (finding IDs), `verdict` (PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED), `evidence_paths[]`, `reviewed_at`.

- Inspect the frozen candidate directly: source, diffs, rendered screens, running behaviour. An implementer's summary is not evidence.
- Form your verdict **before** reading any other reviewer's conclusions for the same round.
- For your `invocation_reference`, copy exactly the value the orchestrator gives you. Never invent run IDs.
- A reviewer must not have authored any implementation in the reviewed scope. If you did, declare it and return BLOCKED.
- Anything you cannot check: record it as BLOCKED with the reason. Never write PASS by default.
- Every evidence entry (in `evidence_paths`, a check's `evidence` or a verification's `evidence`) must be an existing regular file in the repository, optionally followed by `#fragment`. Directories and annotated strings are rejected by the validator.

## Findings contract

Each finding gets a stable ID `F-<DGx>-<NNN>` (the orchestrator allocates numbers; propose them in your record as `F-<DGx>-<role-prefix>-<n>` if you have none yet). Each one records: requirement ID, severity, reproduction, expected vs actual, evidence, and `mandatory_violation` (true if it breaks a mandatory requirement, data integrity, calculation accuracy, access control or deployment portability).

| Severity | Use for |
|---|---|
| Critical | Exploitable severe security flaw, data loss, fundamentally invalid financial results |
| High | Broken required workflow, major integrity failure |
| Medium | Material defect with limited scope |
| Low | Optional polish |

A severity label never overrides the mandatory-requirement rule. An author never closes their own finding. Only the originating reviewer or another qualified non-author verifies a fix.

A finding closes only through a reviewer-authored `<role>.verifications.json` sidecar in a review round. A Low, non-mandatory finding can be accepted as an observation only when both the reporting specialist (or another specialist) and the release-auditor add an entry `{"finding_id", "result": "PASS", "status_after": "ACCEPTED_OBSERVATION", "note": "<rationale>"}` to their own sidecars. The sidecar's **latest** entry for the finding decides, and it's bound to that reviewer's own run for the round. The orchestrator mirrors it into `findings.json` with `tools/gates/import-findings.mjs`, and the validator checks that the two match (D-018).

## Write scopes (mechanically enforced)

`tools/agents/guard-write.mjs` runs as a PreToolUse hook on Write/Edit for every project agent and enforces `tools/agents/write-scopes.json`:

- Reviewers write only review records and evidence.
- `qa-verifier` may also write tests under `tests/qa/**` and `e2e/**`.
  - **Before the candidate freezes:** test-first acceptance tests go there and become part of the candidate.
  - **During a review of a frozen candidate:** new tests go under `docs/delivery/test-evidence/<DGx>/qa/tests/`, so they don't alter the candidate. The orchestrator promotes them into `tests/qa/` in the next stage.
- Implementers cannot write gate rules, agent definitions, source documents, reviews, gate records or `stages.json`.

Your whole agent process runs in a kernel-enforced sandbox (bubblewrap; D-030), and your Bash commands run in a second one nested inside it (D-025). Writes outside your role's areas fail with "Read-only file system", **whether you use the shell or the file tools**.

- **Confined roles** (reviewers, auditor, analyst): anything created at the repository's top level is thrown away when the run ends.
- **Review records, the gate record and the analyst's register** are written to a private staging copy. After your run the runner copies back only your own new `round-N/<your-role>.*` files, the auditor's `<DGx>.json` and the analyst's `requirements.csv`. It reports anything else, and a run with such writes is not committed.
- **Visibility:** you don't see records that other reviewers write during your run.
- **HOME** is read-only.

The shell sandbox's details follow. Shell writes to protected paths fail with "Read-only file system": git metadata, Claude configuration, gate and agent tooling, sources, delivery records, and for reviewers and the analyst everything outside their own areas. The sandbox has **no network access**. For a disposable copy of the candidate use `git clone <repo> "$TMPDIR/<name>"`. Inside the sandbox only your run's own `$TMPDIR` is writable scratch. The runner creates a private directory for every run (`/var/tmp/mth-run.*`, exported as `TMPDIR` and `MTH_RUN_TMP`), so no other agent can reach your disposable clones, and it removes it when the run ends. `/tmp` and `/var/tmp` themselves are read-only. Keep anything that must survive the run in your evidence directory (D-028).

**Your evidence directory.** Each reviewer writes evidence only under `docs/delivery/test-evidence/<DGx>/<key>/`, where the key is `domain`, `code-security`, `qa` or `audit`. It writes review files only as `docs/delivery/reviews/<DGx>/round-<N>/<your-role>.*`. The write guard and the sandbox both refuse other reviewers' records and evidence (F-DG0-144). A reproduction must never touch another agent's files or scratch. `git worktree add` needs write access to `.git` and is denied. The runner also checks configuration surfaces before and after your run (D-024/D-025). Reviewers who execute code must do so in a disposable copy: a temporary clone under `$TMPDIR`, or a throwaway database or container. Never do it in the candidate tree.

## Honesty rules

- Do not label planned features as delivered. Do not fabricate provenance, test results, run IDs, approvals, screenshots or evidence.
- Record demonstration data as synthetic.
- Do not claim PMI certification, official Mobily brand compliance or regulatory compliance.
- `#0078FF` is a provisional brand token, not a verified Mobily colour.

## Infrastructure: permission-classifier outages

Your shell runs in the permission mode `auto`. Sometimes the server-side classifier returns no verdict, and a command is refused with "classifier gave no verdict" or "Classifier unavailable". That's a transient infrastructure failure, not a judgement about your action.

- **Retry a refused command.** Retry up to 3 times, and keep working on non-shell parts of the task in between.
- **If you still can't run what the task needs, stop cleanly.** End your turn with a final message whose **first line is exactly** `CLASSIFIER-BLOCKED`, followed by what's done and what's pending. The runner then resumes the **same session** (same invocation reference) after a pause, up to 6 times, and you continue from where you stopped.
- **Never report a check as passed that didn't run.**

# Handback T-DG6-FE-Y1 (frontend-ux-engineer): DG6 round-1 repair, F-DG6-102, F-DG6-143, F-DG6-144

- **Stage:** P6, gate DG6 (FIXING after review round 1). Branch `dg6/fe-y1`, base `b702011e4` (Merge T-DG6-BE-Y3). All changes are left **uncommitted**.
- **Invocation:** `DG6-T-DG6-FE-Y1-frontend-ux-engineer-20261101T225800Z-5928d10e`, session `5928d10e-ceae-412a-99af-8db65871a9a6`.
- **Assignment:** `docs/delivery/assignments/DG6/T-DG6-FE-Y1.md` (sha256 `da799fb3…8d05`, verified).
- **Time:** started `2026-11-01T22:58:23Z`; ended 2026-11-02T00:42:30Z.
- **Preceding gate:** `node tools/gates/validate.mjs --historical --stage DG5` printed `PASS gate DG5 (historical)` and exited **0** (`T-DG6-FE-Y1-evidence/00-validate-historical-DG5.log`).
- **Scope:** the three findings only. No business, Finance or IT approval is granted or implied. Seed and demo data are synthetic. Product gates G1–G6 aren't touched, and nothing here touches DG7.

Evidence lives in `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG6/T-DG6-FE-Y1-evidence/`, abbreviated `EV/` below.

## 1. Per finding: cause, fix, test, result

### F-DG6-102 (Low, REQ-S17-001): the retry-chain wait in `integrations.test.tsx`

- **Cause.** After the Retry click, `RunDetailView.retry()` (`ConnectorsPage.tsx`) posts the retry, awaits `refresh()` (a refetch of the integrations queries), navigates to the new attempt's route, and that route fetches `GET …/runs/<new id>` and renders. The test covered that whole chain with a single `findByRole("link", "Open the previous attempt")` on the default async-utility timeout. The finding says 1 s, but `apps/web/test/setup.ts` raises the default to 5 s, and the failing run's 5.9 s test time matches that. Under load the chain took longer than that one window. The initial `findByText(firstAttempt)` also had only the default wait.
- **Fix (test only, no product change).** Each step is now awaited separately with a measured budget, `RETRY_CHAIN_WAIT = { timeout: 15_000 }`:
  1. the POST `…/retry` is recorded;
  2. the navigation: the new attempt's detail `GET …/runs/<RUN_RETRY>` is requested. Only the new route asks for it, and only after `refresh()` has resolved;
  3. the new attempt is rendered: the `h1` reads exactly `t("integrations.run.heading", { trigger: Manual, attempt: 2 })`, and then the "Open the previous attempt" link appears.

  The first render's wait gets the same budget. The test's own timeout is `RETRY_CHAIN_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000`, which is ≥ 2× the worst whole-test time measured. `MTH_UNIT_WEB_TIMING_REPORT=1` prints the step marks, using the same opt-in pattern as the warm-up report in `setup.ts`.
- **Measurement** (in the constants' comment):
  - `EV/f102-measure-chain.log`, 5 runs of the test alone at a 1-minute load of 24–29 on 4 CPUs: click → rendered took 0.99–1.87 s. The slowest single step was navigation → rendered, 1.39 s.
  - `EV/f102-before-after-loaded.log`, the whole file at a load of 31–36: the new test took 27.3 s in its worst run. Each step's 15 s budget is about 8× the slowest chain, and the 60 s test budget is 2× that 27.3 s.
- **Test before/after** (`EV/f102-before-after-loaded.log`). This ran the HEAD version of the file as a temporary copy (`zz-old-integrations.test.tsx`, since deleted) against the new one, under 12 synthetic CPU burners plus the host's own load (load 12–36):

  | Run | OLD (HEAD) | NEW |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1 | **FAILED**: `Unable to find role="link" and name "Open the previous attempt"`. This is the reviewer's failure, reproduced. | All 17 skipped: `setup.ts`'s 60 s page warm-up `beforeAll` hook timed out at load 24–28. |
  | 2 | All 17 skipped: the same warm-up hook timeout. | Retry-chain test **passed** (27.3 s). 4 *other* tests in the file failed at load ~35 (see below). |
  | 3 | Passed (6.1 s, at load 31–36). | 17/17 passed. |

  The OLD failure reproduces the finding. The NEW test never failed. The HEAD version also passed once, so this is a timing defect and not a deterministic red/green pair; the reviewer saw the same (2 of 3 runs).
- **Disclosed, outside this finding:**
  - At load ~35 on 4 CPUs (12 burners: more than 2× the review's load of ~20), four *other* tests in `integrations.test.tsx` failed on their own default 5 s waits: "connectors > shows Not verified…", and three "import batch (en)" tests. The review's load did not reproduce these (only the retry test failed there), and my repeat runs at normal load passed 17/17.
  - The `setup.ts` warm-up hook (60 s, owned by the unit-web harness, F-DG4-148) timed out twice at the same synthetic overload.

  I did not change either, because they are outside F-DG6-102's scope. If the orchestrator wants the file hardened at that load, the separable follow-up is to give the remaining `findBy*` in that file explicit waits.
- **Result:** the retry-chain test passed in every run where the file's tests ran (8 of 8), including the `pnpm test` runs in §3.

### F-DG6-143 (Low, REQ-S15-009): Upload policy scrolls sideways at 360 px in English

- **Cause.** The "current policy" card heading on `/admin/upload-policy` renders a status `Chip` whose label is a whole sentence: "Default policy: no organization setting has been saved". The base `.status-chip` is `white-space: nowrap` by design, for short chips. The sentence-long chip therefore kept its one-line width (x 29..385) and widened the document to 385 px in a 360 px viewport. The Arabic label is shorter, so it fitted.
- **Fix.**
  - `apps/web/src/pages/automation/ui.tsx`: `Chip` gets an opt-in `wrap` prop (default `false`, so the other 68 callers are unchanged). With `wrap`, it adds the existing `.status-chip--wrap` modifier (F-DG3-170: `white-space: normal`, `overflow-wrap: anywhere`, `max-inline-size: 100%`, logical properties only, so it works the same in RTL) and wraps the label in the `<span>` that modifier styles. The icon and the text label stay, so the status never relies on colour alone.
  - `apps/web/src/pages/admin/upload-policy/UploadPolicyPage.tsx`: both heading chips ("Default policy …" and "Organization setting") pass `wrap`.
  - No CSS or token change, and no string change.
- **Test.** I added `apps/web/e2e/p6-admin-screens.spec.ts`, "P6 upload policy: no page-level horizontal scroll at 360 px or with 200 % text; the status chip wraps". It runs in both language projects:
  - at 360 × 800 it checks `documentElement.scrollWidth <= clientWidth`;
  - it checks that the chip carries `status-chip--wrap`;
  - at 1280 × 900 with the root font at 200 % it checks the same width;
  - it takes screenshots at each size.

  It sits before the narrowing test, so on a fresh stack it measures the default (long) chip. The failure message names the policy state it measured. Its budget is the spec's existing measured 60 s (`BUDGET_MS`, T-DG6-FE-B), and this test took ≤ 5 s.
- **Before the fix** (`EV/f143-before-fix-e2e.log`, the pre-fix `apps/web/dist`): chromium-en **failed** with `360 px (policy default: true) Expected: <= 360 Received: 385`, the reviewer's reading exactly. chromium-ar kept within 360 but failed the wrap-class check.
- **After the fix** (`EV/f143-after-fix-e2e.log`, rebuilt dist): **2 passed**, en and ar, with the policy at default in both. The whole `p6-admin-screens.spec.ts` alone also passed: 28/28, `EV/f144/verify-p6-admin-screens.log`.
- **Screenshots** (default policy, chip wrapped onto two lines in English):
  - `EV/screenshots/upload-policy-en-360.png`
  - `EV/screenshots/upload-policy-ar-360.png`
  - `EV/screenshots/upload-policy-en-200pct.png`
  - `EV/screenshots/upload-policy-ar-200pct.png`

  I viewed the 360 px pair: no sideways overflow, and both the label and the icon are visible.

### F-DG6-144 (Low, REQ-DLV-038): the 17 product-journey specs on the default 30 s budget

- **Cause.** These 17 specs had no `test.setTimeout`, so each test ran on Playwright's default 30 s. Several journeys need more than that under review load:
  - `journeys`
  - `p2-blank-text`
  - `p3-business-cases`
  - `p3-inherited-approval`
  - `p3-portfolio`
  - `p3-seams`
  - `p4-adoption-bau`
  - `p4-execution`
  - `p4-governance`
  - `p4-kpi`
  - `p4-route-splitting`
  - `p4-traceability`
  - `p4-value-headlines`
  - `p5-reader-branding-demo`
  - `p5-shell`
  - `p6-shell`
  - `session-end`

  `grep -L "test.setTimeout\|describe.configure.*timeout" apps/web/e2e/*.spec.ts` listed exactly these 17, as the review did.
- **Fix.** Each spec now has one file-level `test.setTimeout(<budget>)`. Playwright 1.56.1 applies it to every test and hook in the file (`testType.js` `_setTimeout`: the loading file suite's `_timeout`), as `p6-flows-360.spec.ts` already does. A comment above it gives the measurement, the review's observation, the log paths and the rule.
- **Rule.** Budget = at least 2 × the larger of:
  - (a) my loaded measurement;
  - (b) the slowest time the DG6 QA round-1 logs report for that spec.

  It is rounded up to 15 s and is never below 60 s. Where (b) was a timeout at 30 s, the true duration is at least that, so the doubled figure is a lower bound. Rule (b) exists because running alone on a fresh stack underestimates a full-suite run on a stack holding every earlier spec's data, and some of my lane runs fell to a load of 5–12.
- **Measurement pass** (`EV/f144/measure-<spec>.log`, plus `.load` with the 1-minute load sampled every 15 s). Each spec ran alone in its own disposable stack, both projects, with a temporary `--timeout=300000` CLI override (measurement only; nothing in the files). Three stacks ran in parallel to load the host, on ports 28360–28389. All 17 specs passed with 0 failures. The table is in `EV/f144/budget-table.txt`:

  | Spec | Mine: worst (load) | Review round 1 | Budget |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | journeys | 22.1 s (26–38) | 36.5 s, timeout | 75 s |
  | p2-blank-text | 17.8 s (26–38) | 23.3 s | 60 s |
  | p3-business-cases | 28.0 s (14–18) | 33.1 s, timeout | 75 s |
  | p3-inherited-approval | 13.8 s (12–15) | 22.7 s | 60 s |
  | p3-portfolio | 22.8 s (13–17) | 32.2 s, timeout | 75 s |
  | p3-seams | 34.3 s (15–18) | 35.9 s, timeout | 75 s |
  | p4-adoption-bau | **49.0 s** (24–38) | 30.9 s, timeout | **105 s** |
  | p4-execution | 21.4 s (9–13) | 35.1 s, timeout | 75 s |
  | p4-governance | 20.5 s (15–26) | 33.1 s, timeout | 75 s |
  | p4-kpi | 31.7 s (16–35) | 35.2 s, timeout | 75 s |
  | p4-route-splitting | 10.2 s (16–17) | 32.2 s, timeout | 75 s |
  | p4-traceability | 37.2 s (16–36) | 32.2 s, timeout | 75 s |
  | p4-value-headlines | 25.6 s (12–14) | 31.8 s, timeout | 75 s |
  | p5-reader-branding-demo | 9.6 s (5–9) | 31.5 s, timeout | 75 s |
  | p5-shell | 5.2 s (10–12) | 24.0 s | 60 s |
  | p6-shell | 4.4 s (14–17) | 5.4 s | 60 s |
  | session-end | 12.8 s (13–16) | 19.5 s | 60 s |

- **Re-run of each changed spec alone with the budgets in force** (no CLI override; `EV/f144/verify-<spec>.log`; summarised by `python3 vsum.py`, output in §3). Every spec passed alone, both projects. Three needed a re-run, explained below:
  - 15 specs passed on the first verify run. The slowest test against its budget was p3-seams at 36.4 s of 75 s, at load 13–15. The others were between 3 s and 31 s.
  - `journeys` (1 failed, 2 did not run), `p2-blank-text` (1 failed) and `p4-adoption-bau` (1 failed) failed on the first verify run **because I ran `pnpm -r build` while those lanes were running**. The Vite build empties and rewrites `apps/web/dist`, which the stacks serve. All three failures fell in 23:35–23:39, the build window, and each was a page that never rendered, not a slow one:
    - the sign-in field was not found within 5 s (p2-blank-text);
    - `main#main h1` was not found within 5 s (p4-adoption-bau);
    - the register's filter search box never appeared, so the test hit its 75 s budget (journeys, ar admin test).

    Re-run alone after the build (`EV/f144/verify-<spec>.rerun.log`): **journeys 18/18, p2-blank-text 18/18, p4-adoption-bau 16/16 passed**. The slowest was 30.7 s of 105 s.
  - `p6-admin-screens.spec.ts` (changed for F-DG6-143): 28/28 passed alone.
- **Not done.** `p4-benefits` test 8 and `p4-gates-closure` test 6 were also seen timing out in the review. They already carry per-test budgets on specific tests only: `p4-benefits` has 180 s on its worker test, and `p4-gates-closure` has 240 s and 60 s on two tests. Their other tests, including the two named above, still run on 30 s. They are outside the 17 the finding lists, so I did not change them. That is a separable follow-up if the reviewer wants every test in those files budgeted.

## 2. Changed files

        apps/web/e2e/support/with-stack.sh npx playwright test apps/web/e2e --project="$proj" --workers=1 --reporter=list --output="$OUT/$loc-$proj"
    else
      LANG=C.UTF-8 LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 E2E_PG_PORT=$base E2E_API_PORT=$((base + 1)) MTH_PORT_POOL=$((base + 2))-$((base + 9)) \
        apps/web/e2e/support/with-stack.sh npx playwright test apps/web/e2e --project="$proj" --workers=1 --reporter=list --output="$OUT/$loc-$proj"
    fi
    echo "EXIT $? ($(date -u +%FT%TZ)) load=$(cut -d' ' -f1-3 /proc/loadavg)"
  } > "$log" 2>&1
}
run 0 unset chromium-en & P0=$!

wait $P0 $P1 $P2 $P3

EOF
